card.title: THE BISCUIT BOYS
card.text: Your HQ gets +1 defense when you play a neutral card.
card.flavorText: The “Biscuit Boys” was the nickname of the Royal Berkshire Regiment, whose depot was at Brock Barracks in Reading. In WWII, the regiment fought in France, Burma, Sicily, Italy, and Normandy. The 1st Battalion served with the British Expeditionary Force in 1939 and was evacuated from Dunkirk in 1940. It was later sent to India with the 2nd Infantry Division and fought in Burma under the Fourteenth Army. At Kohima in 1944, B Company helped relieve the 4th Royal West Kents during the siege. The battalion then fought for weeks in difficult conditions, before joining operations around Meiktila and Mandalay later. The 2nd Battalion was already in India when the war began and also served in Burma, notably during the final capture of Mandalay Hill in 1945. The 10th Battalion fought with the 56th London Infantry Division in Sicily and at Anzio, where the fighting became a bitter static struggle. Heavy manpower shortages led to the battalion being disbanded in 1944, with its men sent as reinforcements to other units.
